Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown to the neighbor on My Account. The name is the contract; the sentence is the required wording of the message.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. not-signed-in (INV-CEM-13): a request with no sign-in is refused first.
  2. requester-mismatch (INV-CEM-1): who is asking is settled next, before any other rule.
  3. neighbor-not-found (INV-CEM-10).
  4. email-missing, then email-too-long, then email-invalid (INV-CEM-11, INV-CEM-12).
  5. The new email is the account's current one (INV-CEM-9): succeeds with nothing recorded.
  6. account-closed (INV-CEM-3).
  7. neighbor-suspended (INV-CEM-3a).
  8. email-in-use (INV-CEM-2).
Reason Sentence Rule
not-signed-in Please sign in. INV-CEM-13
requester-mismatch You can only change your own email. INV-CEM-1
neighbor-not-found There is no such neighbor. INV-CEM-10
email-missing Please enter your email address. INV-CEM-11
account-closed This account is closed. INV-CEM-3
neighbor-suspended You can't change your email while your account is suspended. INV-CEM-3a
email-too-long Your email address can be at most 254 characters. INV-CEM-12
email-invalid Please enter a valid email address. INV-CEM-12
email-in-use That email address can't be used. INV-CEM-2

neighbor-not-found can only come from a faulty caller, not from the screen. A missing or malformed neighbor ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked. It is not a refusal and has no reason name. email-missing, email-too-long, email-invalid, email-in-use, account-closed and neighbor-not-found mean the same conditions as in Register Neighbor and Check Out Tool. email-in-use is one reason for every case of INV-CEM-2, worded to be true in each, so a refusal never reveals another account's status; its sentence fits a change rather than a sign-up.

Idempotency: there is no request ID. A request whose effect has already happened, because the account's current email is already the one asked for, succeeds and records nothing (INV-CEM-9).

Requests at the same moment: the email check and the recording of Neighbor Email Changed happen as one step, shared with Register Neighbor, so no two accounts are ever given the same email. Of two requests for the same email at once, from a sign-up or a change, at most one is recorded; the other is refused with email-in-use.

There are no retries, compensations or external calls in this slice. Nothing is emailed when the email changes.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: a neighbor may change only their own email (INV-CEM-1); the shed manager doesn't change neighbors' emails. Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the acting neighbor's ID; a request whose neighbor ID isn't the signed-in neighbor's is refused requester-mismatch.
  • PII & compliance: Neighbor Email Changed holds the neighbor's new email address. The old address stays in the earlier events as the shed's record. Names and emails are kept with the shed's history and never erased.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the one-at-a-time email check above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Neighbor Registered (Register Neighbor): neighborId, email.
    • Neighbor Email Changed (this slice): neighborId, email.
    • Neighbor Suspended (Suspend Neighbor): neighborId. Used for INV-CEM-3a (this neighbor's own suspension).
    • Neighbor Reinstated (Reinstate Neighbor): neighborId. Used for INV-CEM-3a.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId, whileSuspended.
    • These match slices/register-neighbor.md, slices/suspend-neighbor.md and slices/reinstate-neighbor.md. Close Account is specified in a slice being written in depth; it is checked against these keys when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: My Account, Neighbors, Overdue Loans To Notify, Pickup Notices To Send, Undelivered Notices, Flagged Neighbors and Suspended Neighbors (the email). Register Neighbor and later Change Email requests check the new email as held.

Open Questions

None.

"},{"index":5,"name":"Return Tool","x0":965.76,"x1":1109.76,"docHtml":"

Slice: Return Tool

Intent

Let a borrower bring a tool back and end their loan themselves, from My Loans. The tool is then back in the shed, for the next holder or for anyone to borrow. The return records whether it was late, which is what counts toward a neighbor being flagged.

Trigger & Actor

The borrower, from their own My Loans screen, for one of their own loans. My Loans offers Return on every loan it lists (INV-MYL-12), including overdue loans, loans whose tool was retired while out, and loans of a suspended neighbor. The shed manager does not record returns; a tool that never comes back is recorded lost instead (Record Tool Lost).

Command / Input

Command: Return Tool

A NeighborId or LoanId is a UUID.

Field Type Required Rules / Validation
neighborId NeighborId yes The neighbor returning, who must be the one making the request and the loan's borrower (INV-RET-1).
loanId LoanId yes The loan to end. Must be a loan that has been checked out (INV-RET-11), and still out (INV-RET-2).

There is no field for the tool's condition: nothing about it is recorded on return. A damaged tool is the shed manager's to retire.

Trigger

Triggered by: screen My Loans @Neighbor

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Tool Returned → context Loans Read by: My Loans (the loan drops off), Tool Inventory and Tool Catalog (the tool is back in the shed), Holds To Fulfill (a returned tool with holds waiting), Overdue Loans To Notify and Undelivered Notices (the loan has ended), and Neighbors To Flag and Flagged Neighbors (whether the return was late).

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
loanId LoanId yes From the command.
toolId ToolId yes The loan's tool, from its Tool Checked Out. Carried so views about tools and holds match on the tool directly.
returnedAt Instant yes The UTC moment the event is recorded, set by the system.
returnedOn Date yes Set by the system: the calendar date of returnedAt in the shed's local time zone.
late Bool yes Set by the system: yes when returnedOn is after the loan's due date in force at the moment of return (INV-RET-4).

The event never changes. returnedOn and late are worked out once, by the command's handler, so every view reads the same answer.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Tool Returned ends the loan in My Loans, Overdue Loans To Notify and Undelivered Notices; puts the tool back in the shed on Tool Inventory and Tool Catalog (or drops a tool retired while out); adds a tool with holds waiting to Holds To Fulfill; and gives Neighbors To Flag and Flagged Neighbors a late or on-time return. Each is specified in its own doc, and all are eventually consistent.

Invariants / Business Rules

Once a loan is returned, no overdue notice goes out for it (INV-OLN-4, Overdue Loans To Notify). A returned tool with no holds waiting is available to borrow straight away; one with holds waiting is reserved, and until Hold Fulfilled is recorded only the neighbor at the front of the queue may check it out (INV-CHK-3a, Check Out Tool). Late returns count toward a neighbor being flagged, 3 within 90 days (Neighbors To Flag). Those rules are owned by those slices.

  • INV-RET-1: The borrower returns their own loan themselves, from My Loans.
    • The request must come from the neighbor it names, and the loan must be theirs. Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the acting neighbor's ID; a request whose neighbor ID isn't the signed-in neighbor's is refused requester-mismatch. The shed manager does not record returns.
  • INV-RET-2: Only a loan that is still out can be returned, and only once.
    • A loan ended by the shed manager recording the tool lost can't be returned.
    • A closed account never has a loan out, because an account can't be closed while tools are on loan (INV-CLS-7, Close Account).
  • INV-RET-3: Returning a tool records only Tool Returned.
    • Setting the tool aside for the first waiting hold is a separate system reaction to the return, recorded as Hold Fulfilled (Fulfill Hold).
  • INV-RET-4: A return is late when it happens after the loan's due date: from the start of the day after the due date, in the shed's local time.
    • A return on the due date itself is on time. The due date is the one in force at the moment of return: the latest Loan Extended's dueDate, or Tool Checked Out's if never extended.
    • Tool Returned records the answer as late, with the date of return as returnedOn.
  • INV-RET-5: An overdue loan can be returned.
  • INV-RET-7: A suspended neighbor can return a tool.
  • INV-RET-9: A tool retired while on loan can still be returned.
    • The return ends the loan as usual. The tool stays retired: it doesn't come back into the Tool Catalog or Tool Inventory, and no hold is waiting on it, because retiring it ended its holds.
  • INV-RET-10: Returning a loan that this borrower has already returned succeeds and records nothing.
    • So a double submit, or a retry after a lost response, never records a second return.
  • INV-RET-11: The loan must have been checked out.
  • INV-RET-12: A request with no sign-in is refused before anything else is checked.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Happy path: on-time return, no holds (INV-RET-1, INV-RET-3, INV-RET-4)
    • Given: Ana (N1) has the cordless drill (T1) on loan L1, due 12 October, and no holds are waiting on it
    • When: at 15:00 on 11 October, shed time, Ana returns L1 from My Loans
    • Then: Tool Returned is recorded for L1, with toolId T1, the time it was recorded, returnedOn 11 October, and late no. Nothing else is recorded.
  • Return on the due date (INV-RET-4)
    • Given: L1 is due 12 October
    • When: Ana returns L1 at 23:59 on 12 October, shed time
    • Then: Tool Returned is recorded with returnedOn 12 October, late no.
  • Late return (INV-RET-4, INV-RET-5)
    • Given: L1 was due 12 October, and Overdue Notice Sent has been recorded for it
    • When: Ana returns L1 at 00:05 on 13 October, shed time
    • Then: Tool Returned is recorded with returnedOn 13 October, late yes.
  • Return after an extension (INV-RET-4)
    • Given: L1 was due 12 October, and Loan Extended moved its due date to 19 October
    • When: Ana returns L1 on 15 October
    • Then: Tool Returned is recorded with late no, judged against 19 October.
  • Return with a hold waiting (INV-RET-3)
    • Given: Ana has L1, and Ben's hold on T1 is at the front of the queue
    • When: Ana returns L1
    • Then: Tool Returned is recorded. No Hold Fulfilled is recorded by this command; setting T1 aside for Ben is Fulfill Hold's.
  • Suspended neighbor returns a tool (INV-RET-7)
    • Given: Ana is suspended and has L1 out
    • When: Ana returns L1 from My Loans
    • Then: Tool Returned is recorded for L1.
  • Returning a tool that was retired while on loan (INV-RET-9)
    • Given: Ana has the ladder (T2) on loan L2, and Tool Retired was recorded for T2 while it was out
    • When: Ana returns L2 from My Loans
    • Then: Tool Returned is recorded for L2, with toolId T2. T2 stays retired.
  • The same return twice (INV-RET-10)
    • Given: Tool Returned was recorded for L1
    • When: Ana's same Return Tool request for L1 arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded.
  • Loan already recorded lost (INV-RET-2)
    • Given: Tool Lost was recorded for Ana's loan L3
    • When: Ana asks to return L3
    • Then: refused with loan-ended: "This loan has ended." No event is recorded.
  • Someone else's loan (INV-RET-1)
    • Given: Ana has L1 out
    • When: Ben asks, for himself, to return L1
    • Then: refused with not-your-loan: "You can only return your own loans." No event is recorded.
  • A request in someone else's name (INV-RET-1)
    • Given: Ana has L1 out
    • When: a request from Ben asks to return L1 for Ana
    • Then: refused with requester-mismatch: "You can only return loans for yourself." No event is recorded.
  • Unknown loan (INV-RET-11)
    • Given: no loan has ID L9
    • When: Ana asks to return L9
    • Then: refused with loan-not-found: "There is no such loan." No event is recorded.
  • Not signed in (INV-RET-12)
    • Given: nobody is signed in
    • When: a request for returning a tool arrives
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown to the borrower on the My Loans screen. The name is the contract; the sentence is the required wording of the message.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. not-signed-in (INV-RET-12): a request with no sign-in is refused first.
  2. requester-mismatch (INV-RET-1).
  3. loan-not-found (INV-RET-11).
  4. not-your-loan (INV-RET-1).
  5. If Tool Returned is already recorded for the loan, the request is a repeat: it succeeds and records nothing (INV-RET-10).
  6. loan-ended, if Tool Lost is recorded for the loan (INV-RET-2).
Reason Sentence Rule
not-signed-in Please sign in. INV-RET-12
requester-mismatch You can only return loans for yourself. INV-RET-1
loan-not-found There is no such loan. INV-RET-11
not-your-loan You can only return your own loans. INV-RET-1
loan-ended This loan has ended. INV-RET-2

requester-mismatch and loan-not-found can only come from a faulty or impersonating caller, not from the screen. A missing or malformed ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked. It is not a refusal and has no reason name. The names mean the same conditions as in Extend Loan, and loan-ended uses the same sentence.

Suspension, an overdue loan and a retired tool never stop a return; there is no refusal for them.

Idempotency: a return is identified by its loan. A repeat after the loan was returned succeeds and records nothing. A loan ended by Tool Lost is refused, because returning it would be a different outcome from the one recorded.

Requests at the same moment: each Return Tool is decided against the loan's events as already recorded, one at a time per loan. Of a return and a Record Tool Lost for the same loan at once, whichever is decided first is recorded; the other finds the loan ended (a return then gets loan-ended, or succeeds as a repeat if the first was itself a return).

There are no external calls, retries or compensations in this slice.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: a borrower may return only their own loans (INV-RET-1); the shed manager doesn't record returns. Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the acting neighbor's ID; a request whose neighbor ID isn't the signed-in neighbor's is refused requester-mismatch.
  • PII & compliance: Tool Returned holds no name or email; it records which loan ended, when, and whether it was late.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the one-at-a-time rule above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId, neighborId, dueDate.
    • Loan Extended (Extend Loan): loanId, dueDate.
    • Tool Returned (this slice): loanId.
    • Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId.
    • These match slices/check-out-tool.md and slices/extend-loan.md. Record Tool Lost is specified in a slice not yet written in depth; it is checked against this key when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: My Loans, Tool Inventory, Tool Catalog, Holds To Fulfill, Overdue Loans To Notify, Undelivered Notices, Neighbors To Flag and Flagged Neighbors. Fulfill Hold reacts to a returned tool with holds waiting.

Open Questions

None.

"},{"index":6,"name":"Flag Neighbor","x0":1134.76,"x1":1278.76,"docHtml":"

Slice: Flag Neighbor

Intent

When a neighbor's late returns reach the late-return threshold, record that they crossed it, naming the late returns behind the flag, so the shed manager sees them on Flagged Neighbors and decides whether to suspend them. The system flags; a person decides.

Trigger & Actor

Internally triggered. The Late Return Flagger, a system processor in this slice, acts whenever a neighbor appears on Neighbors To Flag, and issues Flag Neighbor for them with the loans that list gives. It is driven by events, not a schedule: a neighbor joins that list when a late return is recorded. No person flags a neighbor, and there is no screen. The neighbor isn't told; a flag is a prompt for the shed manager, not a penalty.

Command / Input

Command: Flag Neighbor

A NeighborId or LoanId is a UUID. One clock reading is taken when the command is handled. "Today" is that moment's calendar date in the shed's local time zone, and the event's flaggedAt is that same moment.

Field Type Required Rules / Validation
neighborId NeighborId yes The neighbor to flag. Must be a registered account (INV-FLG-10), not closed and not suspended (INV-FLG-5).
loanIds LoanId[] yes The late returns behind the flag, by loan, as Neighbors To Flag gave them. Must be exactly the neighbor's counting late returns today (INV-FLG-4), and at least 3 of them (INV-FLG-2). Order doesn't matter.

Trigger

Triggered by: processor Late Return Flagger, also in this slice, reading Neighbors To Flag.

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Neighbor Flagged → context Neighbors Read by: Flagged Neighbors (the neighbor's entry, flag count and latest flag date, and the late returns behind the flag) and Neighbors To Flag (the named late returns are used up).

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
neighborId NeighborId yes From the command.
loanIds LoanId[] yes From the command: the late returns this flag uses up. At least 3.
flaggedAt Instant yes The UTC moment the event is recorded, set by the system. Shown as the flag date: its calendar date in the shed's local time zone.

The event never changes. It carries the loans, not copies of names or dates; readers find each loan's tool and return date from its own events. A later flag records a new Neighbor Flagged.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Its processor reads Neighbors To Flag (slices/neighbors-to-flag.md). Neighbor Flagged feeds Flagged Neighbors (slices/flagged-neighbors.md) and takes the named late returns off Neighbors To Flag. Both are eventually consistent.

Invariants / Business Rules

A counting late return, for a neighbor today, is a loan of theirs whose Tool Returned has late yes, and which:

  • counts on its return day and the next 89 days: returnedOn is today or one of the 89 days before, in the shed's local time;
  • isn't named by an earlier Neighbor Flagged for them;
  • was returned after their latest Neighbor Reinstated, if any;
  • was not returned while they were suspended.

A tool recorded lost has no Tool Returned, so it never counts. Once flagged, the neighbor appears on Flagged Neighbors and stays there until the shed manager acts; there is no dismiss action (Flagged Neighbors owns how it shows). Neighbors are flagged by the system only, through the processor above.

  • INV-FLG-2: A neighbor is flagged when they have at least 3 counting late returns.
    • "At least 3" is tested on the neighbor's own counting set, worked out from their events when the command is handled, not on the loans the command names. Loans that don't count are never made up for by naming them.
  • INV-FLG-3: Flagging never suspends anyone.
    • Flag Neighbor records only Neighbor Flagged. The shed manager decides whether to suspend a flagged neighbor (Suspend Neighbor).
  • INV-FLG-4: A flag uses up the late returns that caused it.
    • Neighbor Flagged names, by loan, every counting late return the neighbor has when it is recorded, even if there are more than 3. Those loans never count again.
    • The neighbor is flagged again only after 3 new counting late returns.
  • INV-FLG-5: A neighbor is flagged only while they are still due a flag.
    • A neighbor whose account is closed is never flagged, and nor is a suspended neighbor. A neighbor whose count was reset by reinstatement after they joined Neighbors To Flag is not flagged for those late returns.
  • INV-FLG-7: A neighbor flagged again while an earlier flag is still waiting on Flagged Neighbors gets a second Neighbor Flagged.
    • An earlier flag never stops a new one. Flagged Neighbors keeps one entry for the neighbor, with the count and the latest date.
  • INV-FLG-9: Flagging a neighbor again for exactly the loans an earlier Neighbor Flagged already names succeeds and records nothing.
  • INV-FLG-10: The neighbor must be a registered account.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Happy path (INV-FLG-2, INV-FLG-3, INV-FLG-4)
    • Given: Ana (N1) is active, with late returns of loans L1 on 1 September, L2 on 20 September and L3 on 5 October, none named by an earlier flag. It is 5 October.
    • When: the Late Return Flagger issues Flag Neighbor for N1 with L1, L2 and L3
    • Then: Neighbor Flagged is recorded for N1, naming L1, L2 and L3, with the time it was recorded. Nothing else is recorded.
  • Four counting late returns (INV-FLG-4)
    • Given: Ana has counting late returns L1, L2, L3 and L4, none flagged
    • When: Flag Neighbor is issued for N1 with L1, L2, L3 and L4
    • Then: Neighbor Flagged is recorded naming all four.
  • A loan left out (INV-FLG-4)
    • Given: Ana has counting late returns L1, L2, L3 and L4
    • When: Flag Neighbor is issued for N1 with only L1, L2 and L3
    • Then: refused with late-returns-changed: "The late returns behind this flag have changed." No event is recorded.
  • Below the threshold (INV-FLG-2)
    • Given: Ana has counting late returns L1 and L2 only
    • When: Flag Neighbor is issued for N1 with L1 and L2
    • Then: refused with below-threshold: "This neighbor has fewer than 3 late returns that count." No event is recorded.
  • A late return drops out of the window (INV-FLG-2)
    • Given: Ana's late returns were on 1 June, 20 September and 5 October, none flagged
    • When: Flag Neighbor is issued for N1 on 5 October with all three loans
    • Then: refused with below-threshold: "This neighbor has fewer than 3 late returns that count." The 1 June return is more than 90 days back. No event is recorded.
  • Window boundary (INV-FLG-2)
    • Given: Ana's late returns were on 8 July, 20 September and 5 October, none flagged
    • When: Flag Neighbor is issued for N1 on 5 October with all three loans
    • Then: Neighbor Flagged is recorded: 8 July is the 89th day before 5 October, so it still counts.
  • Flagged again on new late returns (INV-FLG-4, INV-FLG-7)
    • Given: Ana was flagged on 5 October for L1, L2 and L3, and the shed manager hasn't acted. Since then she returned L5, L6 and L7 late, on 20 October, 1 November and 15 November.
    • When: Flag Neighbor is issued for N1 with L5, L6 and L7 on 15 November
    • Then: Neighbor Flagged is recorded again, naming L5, L6 and L7.
  • Used-up returns don't count again (INV-FLG-2, INV-FLG-4)
    • Given: Ana was flagged for L1, L2 and L3, and returned L5 late since
    • When: Flag Neighbor is issued for N1 with L1, L2, L3 and L5
    • Then: refused with below-threshold: "This neighbor has fewer than 3 late returns that count." Only L5 counts. No event is recorded.
  • An old loan named alongside new ones (INV-FLG-4)
    • Given: Ana was flagged for L1, L2 and L3, and has since returned L5, L6 and L7 late
    • When: Flag Neighbor is issued for N1 with L1, L5, L6 and L7
    • Then: refused with late-returns-changed: "The late returns behind this flag have changed." L1 was used up by the earlier flag. No event is recorded.
  • The same flag arrives twice (INV-FLG-9)
    • Given: Neighbor Flagged was recorded for N1, naming L1, L2 and L3
    • When: Flag Neighbor for N1 with L1, L2 and L3 is issued again
    • Then: it succeeds and nothing new is recorded.
  • Suspended neighbor (INV-FLG-5)
    • Given: Ana is suspended, with 3 late returns from before her suspension that were never flagged
    • When: Flag Neighbor is issued for N1
    • Then: refused with neighbor-suspended: "This neighbor is suspended." No event is recorded.
  • Count reset by reinstatement (INV-FLG-5)
    • Given: Ana returned L1, L2 and L3 late, then was suspended and reinstated
    • When: Flag Neighbor is issued for N1 with L1, L2 and L3
    • Then: refused with below-threshold: "This neighbor has fewer than 3 late returns that count." Returns from before her reinstatement don't count. No event is recorded.
  • Closed account (INV-FLG-5)
    • Given: Ana's account was closed after she reached 3 counting late returns
    • When: Flag Neighbor is issued for N1
    • Then: refused with account-closed: "This account is closed." No event is recorded.
  • Unknown neighbor (INV-FLG-10)
    • Given: no account has neighbor ID N9
    • When: Flag Neighbor is issued for N9
    • Then: refused with neighbor-not-found: "There is no such neighbor." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

A refusal records nothing; the Late Return Flagger logs it with the neighbor ID and moves on. No person sees these reasons. The name is the contract; the sentence is the log text.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. neighbor-not-found (INV-FLG-10).
  2. If a Neighbor Flagged for this neighbor already names exactly these loans, the command succeeds and records nothing (INV-FLG-9).
  3. account-closed, then neighbor-suspended (INV-FLG-5).
  4. below-threshold (INV-FLG-2).
  5. late-returns-changed, if the loans given aren't exactly the neighbor's counting late returns (INV-FLG-4).
Reason Sentence Rule
neighbor-not-found There is no such neighbor. INV-FLG-10
account-closed This account is closed. INV-FLG-5
neighbor-suspended This neighbor is suspended. INV-FLG-5
below-threshold This neighbor has fewer than 3 late returns that count. INV-FLG-2
late-returns-changed The late returns behind this flag have changed. INV-FLG-4

neighbor-not-found, account-closed and neighbor-suspended mean the same conditions as in the neighbor commands; the sentences here fit a system log. A missing or malformed ID, or an empty loan list, is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked.

Idempotency: a repeated Flag Neighbor with the same loans succeeds and records nothing (INV-FLG-9). The flagger may act on the same neighbor twice before Neighbor Flagged lands; the second command is then a repeat.

late-returns-changed means the list moved on between the flagger's read and the command, for example a fourth late return landed. The flagger acts again on the list's updated entry, which gives the current set.

Requests at the same moment: Flag Neighbor is decided against the neighbor's events as already recorded, one at a time per neighbor. A suspension, reinstatement or closure landing at the same moment is decided in the same order: whichever is recorded first stands.

There are no external calls, retries or compensations in this slice. Nothing is emailed when a neighbor is flagged.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: only the Late Return Flagger issues Flag Neighbor. No person or screen does. It is an internal automation command, not on the REST API, so it has no sign-in guard.
  • PII & compliance: Neighbor Flagged links a neighbor to loans they returned late. It holds no name or email.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the list's freshness. The flagger acts as soon as the neighbor appears on Neighbors To Flag, shortly after the late return that crosses the threshold is recorded.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Neighbor Registered (Register Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, neighborId.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool): loanId, returnedOn, late.
    • Neighbor Flagged (this slice): neighborId, loanIds.
    • Neighbor Suspended (Suspend Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Reinstated (Reinstate Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • These match slices/register-neighbor.md, slices/check-out-tool.md and slices/return-tool.md. The others are specified in slices not yet written in depth; each is checked against these keys when it is.
  • Read model this slice's processor reads: Neighbors To Flag (slices/neighbors-to-flag.md): each neighbor due a flag, with the loans of all their counting late returns.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: Flagged Neighbors and Neighbors To Flag. Suspend Neighbor is offered on Flagged Neighbors.

Open Questions

None.

"},{"index":7,"name":"Flagged Neighbors","x0":1303.76,"x1":1447.76,"docHtml":"

Slice: Flagged Neighbors

Intent

Shows the shed manager every neighbor the system has flagged for repeated late returns, on the Flagged Neighbors screen they suspend neighbors from. The system flags; the shed manager decides. Each entry shows who the neighbor is, how often and when they were last flagged, and the late returns behind the flags.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: the shed manager, opening the Flagged Neighbors screen.
  • What it shows: one entry per neighbor currently flagged, built from the events listed under Read Model / View. Nothing on this screen records anything by itself; its one action issues a command owned by another slice:
    • Suspend (Suspend Neighbor slice), offered on every entry (INV-FLN-5). There is no dismiss action.
  • Flagging is done by the system (Flag Neighbor). A neighbor is not told they were flagged, and a suspended neighbor is never flagged (Neighbors To Flag, INV-NTF-7).

Read Model / View

  • View: Flagged Neighbors built from events: "Neighbor Flagged", "Neighbor Registered", "Neighbor Email Changed", "Tool Added", "Tool Checked Out", "Loan Extended", "Tool Returned", "Neighbor Suspended", "Neighbor Account Closed"
  • Consumed by: the Flagged Neighbors screen (Shed Manager)
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual. An entry appears, changes or drops off shortly after its event is recorded (seconds, not minutes). Suspend checks its own rules when it runs.

One row per flagged neighbor. NeighborId, LoanId and ToolId are UUIDs. A Date is a calendar date in the shed's local time zone; an Instant is a UTC instant set when the event was recorded.

Field Type Source / Notes
neighborId NeighborId Neighbor Flagged.neighborId.
name Text Neighbor Registered.name for neighborId. Never changes.
email Text Neighbor Registered.email for neighborId, replaced by each Neighbor Email Changed.email. Always the current one.
flagCount Int Derived: the number of Neighbor Flagged recorded for the neighbor since their entry appeared (INV-FLN-3).
latestFlaggedAt Instant Derived: flaggedAt of the neighbor's latest Neighbor Flagged. Shown as a date in the shed's local time zone.
lateReturns LateReturn[] Derived: one item for each loan named by the entry's Neighbor Flagged events, as below.

Each LateReturn item:

Field Type Source / Notes
loanId LoanId One of Neighbor Flagged.loanIds.
toolName Text Tool Added.name for the loan's tool (Tool Checked Out.toolId).
dueDate Date The loan's due date in force when it was returned: Tool Checked Out.dueDate, replaced by each Loan Extended.dueDate for the loan.
returnedOn Date Tool Returned.returnedOn for the loan.
flaggedAt Instant flaggedAt of the Neighbor Flagged that named this loan.

To fill an entry when its flag lands, the view also keeps, beyond its rows: every neighbor's name and current email; every tool's name; and, for every loan, its tool, borrower, current due date and return date. These are bookkeeping, not rows, and are never returned.

When an entry appears and drops off.

  • Neighbor Flagged creates the neighbor's entry, or adds to it if they are already listed.
  • Neighbor Suspended removes the entry, whichever screen the suspension came from.
  • Neighbor Account Closed removes the entry.

Queries

  • List flagged neighbors. Takes nothing. Returns every entry with all the fields above, including its late returns. There is no paging. Entries are listed by name, then by when the entry was created: the flaggedAt of its first flag (INV-FLN-10).

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-FLN-1: A neighbor appears on Flagged Neighbors when Neighbor Flagged is recorded for them.
    • Being on this list never suspends anyone by itself.
  • INV-FLN-2: Each entry shows the neighbor's name and current email, the date of their latest flag, and the late returns behind every flag on the entry, each with the tool's name, its due date, the date it was returned, and the date of the flag that named it.
    • The name comes from Neighbor Registered. The email is the current one: Neighbor Registered sets it, Neighbor Email Changed replaces it.
    • Neighbor Flagged names the late returns it uses up, as the loans they belong to. It carries no copies of names or dates. The view looks those loans up in the loan events it hears: the tool from Tool Checked Out and its name from Tool Added, the due date from Tool Checked Out as moved by any Loan Extended, and the return date from Tool Returned.
  • INV-FLN-3: A neighbor has at most one entry. If they are flagged again while still listed, the entry shows how many times they have been flagged, and the latest flag date.
    • An entry starts fresh. A neighbor who leaves the list (suspended), is reinstated and is later flagged again gets a new entry, flagged once, with only the new flag's late returns.
  • INV-FLN-4: A flagged neighbor stays on the list until they are suspended or close their account.
    • There is no dismiss action. A flag the shed manager decides not to act on stays on the list.
  • INV-FLN-5: Every entry offers Suspend, and a suspended neighbor leaves the list.
    • A flagged neighbor suspended from the Neighbors screen leaves this list too.
  • INV-FLN-6: When a flagged neighbor closes their account, they leave the list.
    • Closed is final, so the shed manager is never offered Suspend on a closed account.
  • INV-FLN-10: Entries are listed by name, ignoring case, then by when the entry was created.
    • The same order as every list in the shed.
  • INV-FLN-9: Applying the same event twice leaves the list as if it had been applied once.
  • INV-FLN-11: Only the shed manager can read Flagged Neighbors.
    • A signed-in caller without the shed-manager role is refused with not-shed-manager, and a caller with no sign-in with not-signed-in. Nothing is returned to either.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

Unless a scenario says otherwise: Ana Ruiz registered with ana@example.org. She returned the ladder (L1, due 31 August) on 1 September, the drill (L2, due 15 September) on 20 September and the hedge trimmer (L3, due 1 October) on 5 October, all late.

  • Neighbor flagged (INV-FLN-1, INV-FLN-2, INV-FLN-5)
    • Given: Flagged Neighbors is empty
    • When: Neighbor Flagged is recorded for Ana on 5 October, naming L1, L2 and L3
    • Then: Flagged Neighbors lists Ana Ruiz, ana@example.org, flagged once, latest on 5 October, with three late returns: the ladder (due 31 August, returned 1 September), the drill (due 15 September, returned 20 September) and the hedge trimmer (due 1 October, returned 5 October). Suspend is offered.
  • Due date after an extension (INV-FLN-2)
    • Given: L2 was extended from 15 September to 18 September before it was returned on 20 September
    • When: Neighbor Flagged is recorded for Ana, naming L1, L2 and L3
    • Then: the drill's late return shows due 18 September, returned 20 September.
  • Flagged again while still listed (INV-FLN-3)
    • Given: Flagged Neighbors lists Ana, flagged once on 5 October, and she has since returned three more tools late (L4, L5, L6)
    • When: Neighbor Flagged is recorded for Ana on 15 November, naming L4, L5 and L6
    • Then: Flagged Neighbors still lists Ana once: flagged twice, latest on 15 November, with all six late returns: L1, L2 and L3 flagged 5 October, and L4, L5 and L6 flagged 15 November.
  • Flagged again after reinstatement (INV-FLN-3)
    • Given: Ana was flagged, then suspended, which removed her entry, and later reinstated
    • When: Neighbor Flagged is recorded for Ana on 20 January, naming L7, L8 and L9
    • Then: Flagged Neighbors lists Ana in a new entry: flagged once, latest on 20 January, with only L7, L8 and L9.
  • Flagged neighbor suspended (INV-FLN-5)
    • Given: Flagged Neighbors lists Ana and Ben
    • When: Neighbor Suspended is recorded for Ana
    • Then: Ana leaves Flagged Neighbors. Ben is still listed.
  • Flagged neighbor closes their account (INV-FLN-6)
    • Given: Flagged Neighbors lists Ana
    • When: Neighbor Account Closed is recorded for Ana
    • Then: Ana leaves Flagged Neighbors.
  • Flag left alone (INV-FLN-4)
    • Given: Flagged Neighbors has listed Ana since 5 October, and the shed manager has not suspended her
    • When: a month passes with no Neighbor Suspended recorded for Ana
    • Then: Ana is still listed.
  • Flagged neighbor changes their email (INV-FLN-2)
    • Given: Flagged Neighbors lists Ana Ruiz, ana@example.org
    • When: Neighbor Email Changed is recorded for Ana, to ana.ruiz@example.net
    • Then: Flagged Neighbors lists Ana Ruiz, ana.ruiz@example.net. Her flags are unchanged.
  • Same event applied twice (INV-FLN-9)
    • Given: Flagged Neighbors lists Ana, flagged once
    • When: the same Neighbor Flagged for Ana is applied again
    • Then: Ana is still listed once, flagged once.
  • Listing order (INV-FLN-10)
    • Given: Flagged Neighbors lists Ben Ito (first flagged 1 October) and Ana Ruiz (first flagged 5 October)
    • When: the shed manager lists flagged neighbors
    • Then: Ana Ruiz comes first, then Ben Ito.
  • Listing flagged neighbors
    • Given: Flagged Neighbors lists Ana and Ben
    • When: the shed manager's screen lists flagged neighbors
    • Then: both entries are returned with all their fields and late returns, with no paging.
  • A neighbor tries to read the list (INV-FLN-11)
    • Given: Flagged Neighbors has entries
    • When: a neighbor, signed in without the shed-manager role, asks for the flagged neighbors
    • Then: refused with not-shed-manager: "Only the shed manager can see this screen." Nothing is returned.
  • No sign-in (INV-FLN-11)
    • Given: Flagged Neighbors has entries
    • When: a caller with no sign-in asks for the flagged neighbors
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." Nothing is returned.

Alternate & Error Flows

  • Read refusals: the list query refuses a caller without the shed-manager role with not-shed-manager ("Only the shed manager can see this screen."), and a caller with no sign-in with not-signed-in ("Please sign in."). Nothing is returned on a refusal. These mean the same conditions as in the shed manager's commands.
  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-FLN-9).
  • Events after an entry is gone: once an entry has been removed, a later Neighbor Suspended or Neighbor Account Closed for that neighbor changes nothing. A later Neighbor Flagged starts a new entry.
  • Stale actions: Suspend offered on the screen can be out of date by the time it is used (for example, on a neighbor who has just closed their account). Suspend Neighbor checks its own rules and refuses with its own reason; this view raises no errors of its own.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: the Flagged Neighbors screen is the shed manager's alone. Sign-in, handled outside the shed's events, supplies the shed-manager role; only a caller with it may read this view.
  • PII & compliance: shows flagged neighbors' names, current emails and their late-return history to the shed manager only. An entry is removed when the neighbor is suspended or closes their account. To fill entries, the view keeps every neighbor's name and current email, every tool's name, and every loan's tool, borrower and dates, whether or not they are flagged. Names and emails are kept with the shed's loan and hold history and never erased.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Neighbor Flagged (Flag Neighbor): neighborId, loanIds (LoanId[]), flaggedAt.
    • Neighbor Registered (Register Neighbor): neighborId, name, email.
    • Neighbor Email Changed (Change Email): neighborId, email.
    • Tool Added (Add Tool): toolId, name.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId, neighborId, dueDate.
    • Loan Extended (Extend Loan): loanId, dueDate.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool): loanId, returnedOn.
    • Neighbor Suspended (Suspend Neighbor), Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • These keys match the deep-passed docs. Neighbor Flagged's shape is agreed with slices/flag-neighbor.md.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: none. The screen it feeds issues Suspend Neighbor.

Open Questions

None.

"}],"rowLabels":{"x0":-14.240000000000002,"x1":113.75999999999999}}
